mission: Archive room, Force-locked. Sera's palms on the mechanism; the lock dissolves in seconds from a thousand-year-deep muscle memory. Partial technique lineage fragments; Veranthos named by coordinate and warning notation.
why_now: Each node holds a piece of the picture the fortress archive was missing. This node pays off Sera's era-specific expertise as tactical, not just moral.
conflict: The records reference events and framings Ben has no vocabulary for. Sera translates, and her translation implies a militarised and morally compromised Jedi Lords era that modern Jedi history has quietly trimmed.
turning_point: Sera cracks a Force-lock in seconds that would take modern Jedi years. Her value to the mission becomes undeniable, and Ben's respect shifts from reluctant to genuine.
opening_hook: Sera's hands move over the ancient lock mechanism with the ease of someone unlocking their own front door. A thousand years, and her muscle memory is still better than Ben's training.
closing_hook: The records name Veranthos — coordinates, purpose, and a warning notation Ben can now read. The wound is real. It has a location. And Veraine knows where it is.
emotional_trajectory: Intellectual curiosity -> uncomfortable historical reckoning -> focused urgency

stakes.personal: Ben's growing understanding that modern Jedi education is radically incomplete
stakes.interpersonal: Sera earning her place through competence, not just historical authority
stakes.external: Each fragment of lineage data makes the wound more comprehensible — and more frightening

setting: Battlefield Node bunker — records room, Force-locked archive
sensory_details: The Force-lock dissolving under Sera's touch with the domestic ease of a household latch; holographic records in an older data format; the thin place making concentration work — vision and attention pulling at a slight angle
action_beats: Sera places her palms on the ancient Force-lock and dissolves it in seconds — muscle memory from a thousand years ago
Ben scrolls through holographic records in an archaic data format while Sera translates the terminology
Sera pulls up the Veranthos entry — coordinates, purpose, and a warning notation glowing on the display
notes: R05 continues — technique lineage progressive revelation. Sera's Force-lock skill is her primary tactical contribution — keep it understated, almost domestic; the point is that the lock submits to muscle memory that predates modern Jedi training. Diagnostic-voice trap — Ben should not, in this scene, theorise why the modern Order has forgotten this material. He notices the missing registers and keeps moving. Voice: Zahn-procedural in the archive, one permitted Stover-interior beat when Ben reads the Veranthos warning notation and recognises the place-name in his body before his brain catches up. Anti-pattern: do not have Sera narrate what the Jedi Lords were — the record excerpts should imply it.
